newsitem.title: USA: CME May lumber ends limit down for second day.
newsitem.headline: CME May lumber ends limit down for second day.

text.p: May CME lumber futures ended down the $10.00 per tbf daily limit for the second day as weak cash and technicals again pressured the market, traders said.
Lumber closed off the daily limit to $2.10 per tbf lower with May down the limit at $356.70. Limitless March ended $3.40 lower at $361.60 per tbf.
Trading limits will be expanded to $15.00 per tbf Tuesday due to the two consecutive limit losses in May.
Carryover sell stops from Friday's limit losses and further fundamental and technical fund pressure followed the weak tone to cash lumber, traders said.

"There's been very little volume traded in the cash since just before Christmas. There's the perception that the saw mills have backlogged unsold wood, both in their re-load and distribution system and at their own mills and they are struggling to find a price where they can move a volume of product and make themselves healthy again," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.
May fell to it lowest level since November 21 and points lower after breaking through chart support Friday.
"We broke four months of support when we traded below $372 in May on Friday," Cunningham said.
